title: Elastic egress translation drift causing DNS aliasing during peering swap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production customer reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS aliasing observed after Dedicated VPC peering resynchronizations. Traffic analysis indicates ephemeral egress translation state (SNAT/egress mapping) can drift during peering handoffs, causing DNS replies to be routed back through a stale resolver binding and appear to originate from the wrong tenant. This ticket tracks triage, short-term mitigation, and a durable fix to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy two Dedicated tenants in same region with peering enabled and shared external resolver path.
2) Generate high-rate ephemeral connections from GPU backend that trigger SNAT allocation and egress mapping.
3) Trigger a peering control-plane failover (simulate route reparenting or apply peering rotating script).
4) Observe DNS responses on the client side; occasionally responses map to resolver IPs that belong to other tenant egress mappings.
5) Correlate with egress-metadata timestamps and NAT table entries to see rebind timing mismatch.
investigation_notes:
- Initial heap of customer logs (support bundle) shows DNS resolution dovetails with peering events within 30s windows.
- Kernel-level conntrack entries show ephemeral NAT ports recycled quickly under burst load; race between NAT teardown and new binding during peering reassign leads to stale mapping being reused for unrelated flows.
- Egress resolver affinity cookie persisted in proxy layer even after route change; control-plane reconciliation delayed in edge router by ~12s.
- No evidence of privileged data exfiltration, but tenant name resolution ambiguity created confusion and a repeated support incident.
root_cause: Race condition between egress translation cleanup and peering route reparenting. Control-plane reconciliation did not invalidate proxy resolver affinity quickly enough, and ephemeral SNAT port reuse allowed cross-assignment of DNS reply tuples to the wrong tenant flow during brief windows after peering swap.
fix_description:
1) Short-term mitigation: enforce eager egress-affinity invalidation during peering flips and add conservative SNAT port retirement grace to avoid immediate reuse for 5s following a peering event.
2) Medium-term fix: add a reconciliation hook in the peering controller to atomically drain and rebind per-tenant egress mappings before announcing route changes; augment conntrack pruning logic to include tenant-id guard.
3) Long-term: refactor egress translation allocator to separate tenant-specific ephemeral port ranges to eliminate cross-tenant reuse under stress.
rollback_plan: If mitigation causes regressions in throughput, revert the eager invalidation flag (config) and fall back to a staged rolling update of edge proxies with per-tenant port range feature disabled until full allocator is ready. RBAC and route policies remain unchanged.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy eager invalidation toggle to canary cluster with 10% of affected Dedicated pods.
2) Monitor resolving errors and connection latencies for 24h; if stable, increase to 50% then 100%.
3) Deploy conntrack-prune patch to edge nodes in parallel with router reconciliation hook.
4) Schedule tenant-specific port-range allocator work in runtime-1.24.
monitoring_plan:
Create dashboard tile: DNS-Resolver-Affinity-Mismatches (counts of resolver IP seen vs expected per-tenant).
Add alert: >5 mismatches in 5m for any tenant => P0 paging.
Instrument conntrack pruning success rate and egress-binding invalidation latency metric. Link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/egress/dns-affinity
